title: Internet routing
source_scope: All 11 Markdown lecture guides present at source_commit; original PowerPoint slide visibility and exam scope were not independently rechecked.
question_identity: question_id is stable within this manifest; source_index is zero-based and question_sha256 fingerprints question text plus ordered options. Verify the fingerprint before applying an index after a source edit.

lessons.title: IP and Internet architecture
learning_goals: Explain the common IP layer and encapsulation.
Distinguish best-effort delivery from guarantees provided at endpoints.

lessons.title: Reading an IPv4 header
learning_goals: Identify the roles of TTL, Protocol, checksum, and fragmentation fields.
Interpret header length and the scope of the header checksum.

lessons.title: Fragmentation and path MTU
learning_goals: Calculate fragment offsets and explain destination reassembly.
Explain why losing one fragment wastes work and why PMTUD needs feedback.

lessons.title: IPv4 addresses, prefixes, and ARP
learning_goals: Distinguish an IP destination from the MAC address of the local next hop.
Explain an ARP cache miss for an on-link or off-link destination.

lessons.title: ICMP, ping, and traceroute
learning_goals: Explain ICMP errors and the TTL mechanism used by traceroute.
Distinguish a missing diagnostic reply from failed packet forwarding.

lessons.title: Getting configuration with DHCP
learning_goals: Follow the Discover, Offer, Request, Acknowledge exchange.
Explain leases, renewal, rebinding, pools, and reservations.

lessons.title: Routing, forwarding, and switching models
learning_goals: Separate control-plane route computation from data-plane forwarding.
Compare datagrams, virtual circuits, and source routing.

lessons.title: CIDR, aggregation, and longest-prefix matching
learning_goals: Explain subnetting and aggregation using variable-length prefixes.
Choose the most specific matching route, including a default route.

lessons.title: Autonomous systems and routing domains
learning_goals: Distinguish stub, multihomed, and transit ASes.
Separate intra-AS routing, eBGP, and iBGP.

lessons.title: Link-state routing and shortest paths
learning_goals: Explain how flooding produces a topology database.
Execute the selection and relaxation steps of Dijkstra's algorithm.

lessons.title: Distance-vector routing and Bellman–Ford
learning_goals: Calculate a route from neighbors' advertised distances.
Compare local distance estimates with a link-state topology map.

lessons.title: Routing loops and poison reverse
learning_goals: Explain count-to-infinity after a route failure.
Distinguish loop prevention, loop mitigation, and TTL expiry.
source_sections: Routing loops, split horizon, and poison reverse

lessons.title: RIP and RIPv2
learning_goals: Interpret RIP's hop-count metric and bounded infinity.
Identify fields in an RIPv2 route entry.

lessons.title: OSPF areas and protocol operation
learning_goals: Explain the backbone, local areas, and area border routers.
Follow database synchronization using the five OSPF packet types.
source_sections: OSPF areas, packets, and operation — supplementary †

lessons.title: Why BGP uses paths and policy
learning_goals: Explain why Internet routing crosses independent policy boundaries.
Use an AS path to understand advertisements and AS-level loop detection.
source_sections: Inter-domain routing and the role of BGP

lessons.title: BGP messages, routing state, and next hops
learning_goals: Trace an advertisement through BGP's conceptual routing state.
Explain UPDATE messages, sessions, and next-hop reachability.

lessons.title: BGP route selection and internal sessions
learning_goals: Compare weight, LOCAL_PREF, AS_PATH, MED, and IGP cost.
Distinguish a BGP preference decision from shortest-path forwarding.

lessons.title: Business relationships and export policy
learning_goals: Apply customer, provider, and peer export rules.
Explain how commercial policy can determine reachability.
source_sections: AS business relationships and export policy

lessons.title: BGP hijacks and route leaks
learning_goals: Distinguish unauthorized origination from an inappropriate route export.
Explain how a more-specific unauthorized prefix can attract traffic.

lessons.title: RPKI and route origin validation
learning_goals: Classify origins as Valid, Invalid, or NotFound using a ROA.
Explain why a valid origin does not authenticate the whole AS path.

lessons.title: ASPA and partial deployment
learning_goals: Contrast provider authorization with origin authorization.
Distinguish specification, availability, and deployment.

lessons.title: Convergence, failures, and stability
learning_goals: Explain how updates and independent policies affect convergence.
Distinguish a responsive route choice from a stable route choice.

lessons.title: BGP wedgies: stable but unwanted routes
learning_goals: Distinguish oscillation from multiple stable routing outcomes.
Explain why topology alone is insufficient to reproduce the supplied wedgie.
